Troughs consistently occur near robust standardized values of −1.0 to −0.9, while peaks range narrowly between 3.8 and 4.0. Noise is low: the signal is smooth with minimal high-frequency jitter; roughness values (0.030–0.032) and curvature (~0.014) are tightly clustered. Amplitude (90th percentile range) stays within 3.9–4.6, reflecting minor scaling differences due to robust standardization offsets (median varies ±0.2). No boundary truncation artifacts are visible; all windows capture complete cycles. Acceptable variation includes: (i) small shifts in absolute level (median ±0.2), (ii) slight asymmetry in downstroke steepness, (iii) negligible trend slope differences, and (iv) peak height variation ≤0.2 units. Crucially, morphology—not absolute x-origin—is conserved across all four candidates.
